page: Microsoft Azure E16pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the EPDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The architecture allocates one thread per core, providing a total of 16 vCPUs. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB of memory per core, and includes a 614 GB local SSD.

Performance benchmarks place this server in the average tier for most multi-core and memory-bound operations. The single-core stress-ng performance is 1822.69, while multi-core performance reaches 28904.71. Memory bandwidth tests show 1127.57 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 122.17 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-threaded tasks show some limitations, with a weak Geekbench single-core score of 1087.0 and a weak Passmark CPU encryption score of 2590.42.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the E16pds_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require x86-specific instruction sets. The inclusion of 614 GB of local SSD storage combined with an average Passmark database operations score of 10869.44 and Redis SET performance of 21.74 million operations per second makes it suitable for database hosting, caching layers, and memory-optimized web serving.
